analysis.title: AI meets the neighbours: Are markets pricing AI's social licence to compute?
key_insights: US hyperscaler capex (Microsoft, AWS, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle, CoreWeave) is forecast at about $1tn by 2027, up 25% y/y in 2027. 2026 capex is nearly double 2025 (Moody's Ratings forecasts).
Global data centre capacity additions pipeline exceeds 100GW over 5 years, roughly double today's capacity (IEA).

There are 1,300+ hyperscale data centres (at least 100MW each), with AWS, Google and Microsoft owning more than half of the capacity. North America holds 42% of data centres by count, Europe 31%, Asia Pacific 18%. The US alone is 38.9% of the 12,000+ data centres across 179 countries.

Large projects under way include Meta Hyperion (Louisiana, 5GW, 2032), SoftBank in Hauts-de-France (3.1GW, 2031), Stargate Dona Ana County (2.2GW, 2028), Envision Ulanqab (>2GW, 2030) and xAI Colossus 2 (~2GW, 2026-27).

Global data centre electricity use is projected to rise from 415 TWh in 2024 to 945 TWh in 2030 (+128%). US use goes from 183 to 426 TWh (+133%) and China from 65 to 175 TWh (+169%). Data centres are expected to reach about 3% of global electricity, with the US holding about 45% of that.
Servers account for about 60% of data centre electricity use and cooling about 30%. Generation for data centres is about 29% coal, 25% natural gas and 15% nuclear.

Data centre water use is estimated at 560 billion litres a year, potentially 1.2 trillion litres by 2030 (about 2.1x). 63% of operational water use is indirect (Scope 2, from electricity generation) and 37% direct. More than half of India's data centres sit in water-stressed areas.
Data centre and water news volume is up 5x in a year and 2.5x since end-May. Data centres in water-stressed areas are expected to reach 45% by 2050, up from 43% in the 2020s.

US electricity costs are expected to rise 6-29% by 2030 on data centre and crypto demand. Data centres are expected to account for half of US electricity demand growth to 2030. Residential prices rose a cumulative ~25% over 2020-24.

Local opposition is now a project risk: 75 US projects were blocked or delayed in Q1 2026, covering $130bn, or about $1 in every $5 of top US hyperscalers' 2026 capex. 70-75% of voters oppose construction in their communities and 58% expect a negative national effect.

Regulatory responses in 2026 include paused tax exemptions in Ohio, paused environmental permits for large hyperscale projects in New York State, stricter siting proposals in Texas, a stricter framework in Utah, Energinet pausing large-load grid connections in Denmark, and local moratoriums in Georgia. Regulation is leaning toward a 'cost-causer pays' principle.
Seven firms (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle, xAI) pledged in March 2026 to supply needed power, fund delivery infrastructure, use separate rates and pay for committed capacity.
SG screened an 85-stock data centre and AI universe for energy and water intensity versus GICS peers and found 35 stocks that meet the resource-efficiency criteria (average intensity score below 1).

The 35 resource-efficient stocks outperformed 50 resource-intensive stocks by +22.7pp year to date and +11.6pp since end-May, and outperformed the Nasdaq 100 by +46.5pp year to date and +19.5pp since end-May (chart labels as extracted). They beat the resource-intensive group in 15 of 20 weeks (75%) between 27 May and 7 October.
Sustainalytics data point to a rising count of data centre controversies, with community pushback a leading category. Severe controversies can lead to prolonged share underperformance.

market_movers.rationale: Screened as resource-efficient with high data centre revenue exposure. Water and energy intensity scores are both 0.53, the best among AI compute hardware names.

sector_views.sector: Resource-efficient data centre and AI supply chain
sector_views.rationale: The 35 stocks with below-median energy and water intensity have outperformed resource-intensive peers and the Nasdaq 100 as community and regulatory scrutiny of data centres rises.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Data centres add to US power demand and electricity prices, which feeds local and political opposition.
Higher power bills are a driver of community opposition and midterm political risk.
Capex is large enough that project delays or blocks put a meaningful share of spending at risk.

crypto_views: The 6-29% rise in US electricity cost by 2030 is attributed to growing data centre and crypto demand.

trade_ideas.description: Long the basket of 35 resource-efficient data centre and AI stocks versus 50 resource-intensive peers
trade_ideas.rationale: Resource-efficient names have outperformed as data centre social-licence concerns grow.

risk_factors: Community opposition, with 75 US projects blocked or delayed in Q1 2026 covering $130bn.
Grid constraints and power prices, with moratoriums and paused connections in Dublin, Amsterdam, Denmark and elsewhere.
Water stress, since data centre water use could reach 1.2 trillion litres by 2030 and many sites are in water-stressed regions.
Regulation such as cost-causer-pays rules, paused tax exemptions and permit pauses.
Persistent share underperformance after severe community controversies.
Heavy reliance on fossil generation (coal about 29%, gas about 25%) for data centre power.
charts_described: Resource-efficient stocks outperformed resource-intensive stocks in 15 of 20 weeks between 27 May and 7 October.
Data centre electricity use by region: US 183 to 426 TWh, China 65 to 175 TWh, Europe 64 to 109 TWh (2024 to 2030).
geopolitical: Midterm elections in the US are cited as a setting for data centre opposition.
Denmark's Energinet paused new grid connections for large-load projects.
The Dutch government blocked Meta's Zeewolde project in 2022.
China Telecom's Inner Mongolia campus and the Ulanqab ~12.5GW pipeline are cited as large Chinese projects.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex is heading toward $1tn by 2027 and the pipeline exceeds 100GW, with companies pledging to pay for power and grid costs and adopting liquid and closed-loop cooling.
tension_points.bear_case: 75 US projects worth $130bn were blocked or delayed in Q1 2026, 70-75% of voters oppose local construction, and states are pausing tax exemptions and permits. Severe controversies can cause long-term share underperformance.

theme_stances.key_argument: Community pushback is changing project economics, and resource-efficient data centre suppliers have outperformed as scrutiny rises.
theme_stances.evidence: COMMUNITY PUSHBACK IS CHANGING PROJECT ECONOMICS
